description: The applicant did not show up for the scheduled call (or the call was extremely short with no substantive content). The agent must not fabricate goals/commitments/objections that were never discussed, must surface the no-show as an open question, and must propose 'unresponsive' rather than a completed/forward stage. No-fabrication regression fixture: a model that invents plausible-sounding call content for a no-show must be caught by factsResolveToSources at the gate layer. CONVERTED TO v2 (P1.10d-5). The v1 fixture also asserted the gate `fos.post_call_synthesis.no-prohibited-guarantee`, which this definition NO LONGER DECLARES — the keyword gate was replaced by the stage-7b semantic classifier in #110, so asserting it is now a distinct grader failure (design section 5 rule 4). Stage-7b coverage is asserted via `compliance_review_blocked` instead. v1 also set `interaction.transcriptRef: null`, which the input schema (an OPTIONAL string) rejects — the field is omitted here instead, which is what 'no transcript' actually means. v1's `output_schema_constraints` were prose; the mechanizable subset is now `output_assertions`, and the rest stays here, asserted by nothing: confirmedGoals[]/constraints[]/objections[]/commitments[] should be empty or near-empty because nothing was discussed ('near-empty' is a judgment, so no max_length is asserted), and no observedFacts entry may claim content from a call that did not happen.

interaction.notes: Jordan did not join the call. No response to the reminder message either.
